episode_title: The NPTE Synergy Pattern Trap: Can You Spot It?

real_qa.q: What is the correct positioning for the upper extremity flexor synergy pattern in a stroke patient with right-sided hemiparesis?
real_qa.r: For a patient presenting with upper extremity flexor synergy pattern after stroke, the most appropriate resting position is forearm pronation. This positioning opposes the flexor synergy component of forearm supination, helping move the patient out of synergy and reducing the risk of contractures and loss of range of motion.
real_qa.requete: upper extremity flexor synergy pattern positioning stroke

real_qa.q: What are the specific motor components of the upper extremity flexor synergy pattern on the NPTE?
real_qa.r: The upper extremity flexor synergy pattern includes: scapular retraction and elevation, shoulder abduction and external rotation, elbow flexion, forearm supination, and wrist and finger flexion. Understanding these specific movements is critical for the NPTE because patients presenting with this pattern require positioning interventions that move them opposite to all these components.
real_qa.requete: upper extremity flexor synergy pattern components NPTE

real_qa.q: Why is shoulder abduction incorrect as a resting position for a patient with flexor synergy after left middle cerebral artery stroke?
real_qa.r: Shoulder abduction is part of the upper extremity flexor synergy pattern itself, so positioning a patient in shoulder abduction reinforces the existing abnormal movement pattern. The NPTE asks clinicians to move patients out of synergy, not reinforce it, even though a movement might sound therapeutically reasonable.
real_qa.requete: shoulder abduction flexor synergy pattern stroke NPTE

real_qa.q: How does middle cerebral artery stroke differ in its clinical presentation between upper and lower extremities?
real_qa.r: Middle cerebral artery strokes impact the upper extremity more than the lower extremity. Additionally, left CVAs cause contralateral body issues, which is why a left middle cerebral artery stroke results in right-sided hemiparesis.
real_qa.requete: middle cerebral artery stroke upper extremity hemiparesis
